posts.note: Omakase-vs-a-la-carte essay on two TMS CPT coding proposals before the AMA CPT Editorial Panel. Two scheduled-event/deadline statements and one borderline habitual 'will' logged. Disclosures: Radial co-founder, Ampa Health advisor, Neurolief CMO.
2022 essay reposted with a 2026 intro after the Tate brothers' Miami arrest. Mostly past analysis and normative calls about NPD; one borderline hedge on a reported fact logged.
Podcast intro with Firefly Neuroscience's Dave DeCaprio. Own-practice EEG adoption intent, a general EEG adoption hedge, and a live-event announcement.
Narrative essay about a restraint at Bellevue; only the RAMHT event announcement is forward-looking. 'Picks winners' boast is past-pattern, not logged.

Long interview with Mark Horowitz (Outro Health; author is an advisor). Horowitz's statements are present/past analysis, not forecasts; author's own lines are questions and present claims. Only the RAMHT event plug logged.

statements.quote: Both proposals go before the AMA’s CPT Editorial Panel (the group that decides what gets a billing code, and therefore what insurance will pay for) this September.
statements.context: Two competing CPT coding proposals for TMS, a bundled 'omakase' one (Tab 92) that would cover accelerated protocols with inter-session intervals and on-site physician time, and an a la carte one (Tab 53), are scheduled to go before the AMA CPT Editorial Panel in September 2026. The panel decides billing codes and therefore what insurance pays for. Post dated 2026-07-16.
statements.note: Plain declarative about a scheduled meeting. Author discloses Radial co-founder (accelerated TMS), Ampa Health advisor, Neurolief CMO; coder may mark CONTROL-adjacent.

statements.quote: There’s an open comment window right now, and it closes August 10.
statements.context: The AMA interested-party comment window on the two TMS CPT coding proposals (Tab 92 omakase, Tab 53 a la carte) closes August 10, 2026. The author urges readers to register as interested parties and comment by that date.
statements.note: Deadline statement about an administrative process; low forecast value.

statements.quote: Some practices want to offer all-day treatment with TMS. Others want to offer only once-a-day treatment. Yet others feature fMRI ! Others still will use EEG to calibrate treatment.
statements.context: In arguing for flexible CPT coding, the author lists the variety of TMS practice models, ending with the claim that some practices will use EEG to calibrate treatment.
statements.note: Borderline: 'will use' sits in a list of present-tense practice descriptions and may be habitual rather than predictive. Logged for recall.

statements.quote: This may or may not prove to be actually true, but it’s pretty hilarious either way.
statements.context: From the 2022 body of the repost: reports said the pizza-delivery video in Andrew Tate's reply tweet to Greta Thunberg gave Romanian authorities his location and led to his arrest. The author hedges on whether that report will prove true.
statements.note: Borderline: a 50/50 hedge on future confirmation of a reported fact, written in 2022 and reposted 2026-07-19. Low forecast value.

statements.quote: But one thing I haven’t routinely done is measure the brain itself as part of clinical care, as companies like Firefly Neuroscience are making possible. That may need to change, is the outcome in my personal brain as a result of this interview.
statements.context: After interviewing Dave DeCaprio (president and COO of Firefly Neuroscience, maker of the Evoke qEEG/ERP system), the author says his own practice of not routinely measuring the brain with EEG in clinical care may need to change.
statements.note: Own-practice adoption intent, hedged. Coder may mark CONTROL (author's own clinical practice).

statements.quote: I haven’t used it in clinical practice yet, but Dave makes a compelling case, and at this point I think it’s only a matter of time.
statements.context: The author expects to eventually use Firefly Neuroscience's Evoke system (quantitative EEG plus event-related potentials, compared against a normative database of over 191,000 sessions) in his own clinical practice.
statements.confidence_phrase: I think it’s only a matter of time
statements.note: Own-practice adoption with open-ended horizon; author is the podcast host interviewing the company's COO. Coder may mark CONTROL.

statements.quote: Brain Medicine, as an emerging specialty, brings change. That change needs to be measured. EEG might be one such tool.
statements.context: General claim that EEG might become a tool for measuring treatment-driven brain change in the emerging specialty the author calls Brain Medicine (interventional psychiatry and neuromodulation).
statements.note: Hedged general adoption call. Middle sentence ('needs to be measured') is normative; the call is the last sentence.
